intro.author: Paul, a prisoner, with Timothy named as co-sender (v. 1)
intro.written: About AD 60–62, during Paul's imprisonment, traditionally in Rome; some scholars suggest Ephesus
intro.audience: Philemon, a believer whose home hosted a church, along with Apphia, Archippus and that congregation (vv. 1–2); Colossians suggests they lived in Colossae
intro.setting: Onesimus, a slave belonging to Philemon, had left his master, possibly after wronging him (v. 18), and had come into contact with Paul, who led him to faith. Paul now sends Onesimus back, apparently along with Tychicus and the letter to the Colossians (Colossians 4:7-9).
intro.purpose: Paul appeals to Philemon to welcome Onesimus back no longer merely as a slave but as a beloved brother in Christ.
intro.bigIdea: The gospel turns a slave and his master into brothers.

outline.title: Thanks for Philemon, and Paul's appeal for Onesimus

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL TO PHILEMON
